title: Western Sahara
blurb: Every place GeoNames records above 500 people in Western Sahara: 27 towns and villages, grouped by region and ordered by population.
d:
Western Sahara is a United Nations–designated non-self-governing territory in north-western Africa. It has a surface area of 272,000 square kilometres (105,000 sq mi). Western Sahara is the only african colonial territory remaining on the UN's decolonization list and has been dubbed "Africa's last colony". With an estimated 600,000 inhabitants, it is the most sparsely populated territory in Africa and the second most sparsely populated territory in the world after Greenland, consisting mainly of desert flatlands.
Francoist Spain previously colonized the territory as the Spanish Sahara until 1975–1976. Spain attempted to transfer its administration to Morocco and Mauritania despite an advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice that those countries had no sovereignty over Western Sahara; a war erupted and the pro-independence Polisario Front proclaimed the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (SADR). Mauritania withdrew its claims in 1979, and Morocco secured de facto control of most of the territory, including all major cities and most natural resources. The SADR established a government-in-exile in Tindouf, Algeria. A UN-sponsored ceasefire agreement was reached in 1991, though a planned referendum monitored by the UN's MINURSO mission has since stalled.
Based on modern GIS spatial mapping and calculations of the Berm's perimeter, approximately 15-20% of the Western Sahara (mainly inland and along the Mauritanian and Algerian borders) is controlled by the Polisario Front and the remaining 80-85% (including almost all of the coast) is controlled by Morocco.  Morocco maintains the Berm, a 2,700 km-long (1,700 mi) wall lined with land mines that splits the territory. The Polisario Front is recognized by the UN as a representative of the people of Western Sahara and is primarily supported by Algeria. The SADR has received partial international recognition and membership in the African Union. Morocco is supported by France and the United States; around two-thirds of the UN member states began expressing support for its autonomy proposal in the 2020s, and the United Nations Security Council in 2025 endorsed negotiating based on the proposal through the resolution 2797.
